questions.q: A school nurse wants to record, for each Class 8 student, just two observations that together show the student is healthy in the sense the WHO uses. Which pair would do it?
questions.a: No illness; feels positive and gets on with classmates
o: No illness; feels positive and gets on with classmates
No illness this term; tops every fitness test in the class
Cheerful most days; has a large group of friends
Calm before every exam; no illness at all this term

questions.q:
The counsellor of a Jaipur school is reading the file of Tanvi, who joined in July.
Nurse's note: 'Height, weight and eyesight normal. No fever, no illness.'
Class teacher's note: 'Sits alone at breaks, will not join group work. Says she feels low most days.'
The office has stamped her card 'Fully healthy - no action needed'. Its follow-up plan is: 'Repeat the nurse's check-up in December. If it is normal again, close the file.'
(a) From the teacher's note, pick one observation that shows her social well-being and one that shows her mental well-being.
(b) What is wrong with the office's stamp?
(c) Find the flaw in the December follow-up plan and redesign it so that it would show whether Tanvi has become healthy.
questions.a: (a) Social: she sits alone and will not join group work. Mental: she says she feels low most days. (b) The office judged only from the nurse's note, i.e. absence of disease. By the WHO definition, health is complete physical, mental and social well-being, and the teacher's note shows her social and mental well-being are poor, so she is not fully healthy and does need help. (c) Flaw: the nurse's check-up looks only at her body, which was already normal, so it would come back normal and the file would be closed even if she is still lonely and low. Redesign: keep the nurse's check for the physical aspect, and add the class teacher's or counsellor's observation of whether she now joins group work and has friends (social) and whether she says she feels positive most days (mental); close the file only when all three aspects are good.
s: Part (a): sits alone/no group work = social; feels low = mental
Part (b): the stamp uses only absence of disease; social and mental well-being are poor
Part (c): the repeat check-up tests only the body, so it cannot show change; a redesigned plan checks social and mental well-being as well

questions.q:
Read three statements about health and happiness.
Statement 1: Being happy helps a person stay active and healthy.
Statement 2: The link runs one way only: good health brings happiness, but happiness does nothing for health.
Statement 3: A healthy person can generally cope better in difficult situations.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: Statements 1 and 3 only
o: Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 1 and 2 only
Statement 3 only
All three statements

questions.q: Arjun has been worried about his exams for two months. He stopped cycling in the evenings and now eats very little. This week he feels tired all day and has lost weight, though a check-up finds no disease. Which statement best explains what is happening?
questions.a: A weak mental aspect is now pulling down his physical aspect
o: A weak mental aspect is now pulling down his physical aspect
His body caused the worry, so treating the body alone is enough
Only his social aspect is weak, as he no longer cycles
Mind and body are separate aspects, so the two are not linked

questions.q:
Mehul has many friends and is cheerful in class, but he skips breakfast most days and sleeps only about four hours a night.
(a) Which aspect of health is Mehul putting at risk?
(b) Using your answer to (a), explain why his good friendships alone do not make him healthy by the WHO definition.
questions.a: (a) His physical well-being (his body is not getting food and rest). (b) The WHO definition needs complete physical, mental and social well-being together. Mehul's social (and mental) well-being look good, but the physical aspect named in (a) is at risk, so he is not completely healthy.
s: Part (a): physical well-being
Part (b): all three aspects must be complete together; one good aspect cannot make up for a weak one

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Since good health improves mood, a student who is unhappy must have a disease of the body.
Reason (R): Health and happiness are closely related; being happy helps us stay active and healthy, and good health also improves our mood.
questions.a: A is false, but R is true
o: A is false, but R is true
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false

questions.q: Two equally fit cricketers in a Nagpur school team lose the inter-school final. Jaspreet talks it over with his teammates and is back at practice the next day. Rohan sulks for a week, snaps at teammates and skips practice. What does this difference best show about health?
questions.a: Health includes coping well in hard times, not just fitness
o: Health includes coping well in hard times, not just fitness
Rohan must have a disease, because healthy people never feel upset
Both are equally healthy, since health means the body works well
Jaspreet is healthier only because he is the better cricketer

questions.q: Dr Rao examines Imran and finds no disease. Imran's mother says: 'The doctor found nothing wrong, so Imran is fully healthy as the WHO defines it.' Is her statement True or False? Give the verdict and the reason.
questions.a: False. The check-up shows only that Imran has no disease, which is about his physical well-being. The WHO defines health as complete physical, mental and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease, so his mental and social well-being must also be good before he can be called fully healthy.
s: Verdict: False
Reason: absence of disease covers only part; mental and social well-being must also be complete

questions.q: A school wellness card gives one tick for each aspect of health in the WHO definition that is in good shape. Neel has had no illness all year and is cheerful and positive, but he has no friends in class and avoids every group activity. His card should show ___ ticks. (Write the number in digits.)

Pallavi, a keen member of her school dance group, breaks her leg and must stay at home for six weeks.
(a) Which aspect of her health is harmed directly by the injury?
(b) Predict one other aspect of her health that may suffer during the six weeks, and explain how the injury leads to it.
questions.a: (a) Physical well-being (the broken leg). (b) Social well-being: she cannot meet her dance group and friends, so she may feel cut off from her peers; or mental well-being: being stuck at home and missing dance may make her feel low or upset. The aspects are linked, so a problem in the body can spread to the other two.
s: Part (a): physical well-being
Part (b): social or mental well-being, with the link from the injury (cut off from friends, feeling low)

questions.q:
Ira changed schools in June. Her diary has three entries.
Week 1: 'Nobody sits with me at lunch. I have no one to talk to.'
Week 2: 'I feel low all the time. Even my favourite songs do not cheer me up.'
Week 5: 'Headaches every day, and my uniform has become loose.'
(i) Name the aspect of health that each entry mainly shows.
(ii) What does the order of the entries show about how the three aspects are linked?
questions.a: (i) Week 1: social well-being (no friends, no one to talk to). Week 2: mental well-being (feeling low, nothing cheers her up). Week 5: physical well-being (headaches, weight loss). (ii) The order suggests (it may show) that the problem began in the social aspect, spread to the mental aspect, and finally showed up in the body. The three aspects are linked, so a gap in one can affect the others; this is why health means all three, not just the absence of disease.
s: Weeks 1 and 2 matched to social and mental well-being
Week 5 matched to physical well-being
The order may show a social problem spreading to the mind and then the body, so the aspects are linked

questions.q: A school wants to find out how its students are doing in every aspect of health named by the WHO. Which check would tell it NOTHING about the students' social well-being?
questions.a: Measuring each student's height, weight and eyesight
o: Measuring each student's height, weight and eyesight
Asking whether students get along with their classmates
Noting which students join group games and class teams
Seeing how students adjust after being moved to a new section

questions.q:
Match each student in Column I with the aspect of health that needs attention in Column II.
Column I | Column II
1. Raju has a fractured wrist from a fall but laughs and chats with his friends as usual | a. Social well-being
2. Meena is fit and has many friends but worries all the time and feels low | b. None; all three aspects are in good shape
3. Sohan is fit and cheerful but cannot adjust with his hostel roommates and keeps to himself | c. Physical well-being
4. Tara eats well, stays positive and enjoys being in her cricket team | d. Mental well-being

Sameer, a class monitor with a large circle of friends, claims: 'I get along with everyone, so I am socially healthy, and that means I am a healthy person.' Is his claim right, wrong or partly right? Explain using the WHO definition.
questions.a: Partly right. Getting along well with others does show good social well-being, so the first half of his claim is sound. But the WHO defines health as complete physical, mental and social well-being, not one of them. Sameer can be called healthy only if his physical and mental well-being are also good, which his claim does not show.
s: Verdict: partly right
Getting along with everyone does show social well-being
Health needs physical and mental well-being too, so the conclusion does not follow

questions.q:
Two Class 8 students of equal ability get the same science project. Lata is free of illness, sleeps well, feels positive and gets on with her group. Vikram has been unwell with a cold for a week, is worried about it, and has fallen out with his group.
(a) According to the chapter, which student is more likely to finish the work efficiently and cope if something goes wrong?
(b) Name the aspects of health in which Vikram is weak this week.
questions.a: (a) Lata. The chapter says a healthy person can generally perform tasks more efficiently and cope well in difficult situations, and Lata is well in all three aspects. (b) Physical (unwell with a cold), mental (worried) and social (fallen out with his group).
s: Part (a): Lata, as a healthy person works more efficiently and copes better
Part (b): physical, mental and social, each linked to his situation

questions.q:
A class teacher notes three students for one term.
Student | Body | Feelings | Relations with others
P | No illness, plays basketball daily | Often anxious before every test, cries easily | Many friends, team captain
Q | Has had asthma attacks twice this term | Cheerful, positive | Gets along well, helps classmates
R | No illness, active | Calm and positive | Quarrels often, has been left out of every group
(a) For each student, name the aspect of health that is weak. (3)
(b) The teacher can send one student to the school doctor and the other two to the school counsellor. Which student should go to the doctor? Justify from the aspect that is weak. (1)
(c) Suggest one helpful step for student R that matches his weak aspect. (1)
questions.a: (a) P: mental well-being (anxiety, crying). Q: physical well-being (asthma attacks). R: social well-being (quarrels, left out of groups). (b) Q, because Q's weak aspect is physical (asthma, a disease of the body), while P's weakness is mental and R's is social, which a counsellor can help with. (c) For R, something that builds relationships, e.g. a counsellor or teacher helping him join a group activity and make friends.
s: P: mental well-being is weak
Q: physical well-being is weak
R: social well-being is weak
Part (b): Q goes to the doctor, since only Q's weak aspect is physical
A step for R that builds social well-being

questions.q: A coach's report on a Class 8 athlete reads: 'When her relay team lost the final, she was the one who calmed the others and planned the next practice. She copes better than her teammates because she is healthy in all three aspects.' Write a short situation (three or four sentences) about this athlete's daily life that would make the report's reason correct. Then explain, using the chapter, why a person healthy in all three aspects copes better in a difficult situation.
questions.a: Example: Neha sleeps well, eats a balanced diet and has no illness. She stays positive even on bad days and talks about her worries with her parents. She gets along with all her teammates and helps new members settle in. Explanation: the chapter says a healthy person can generally perform tasks more efficiently, cope well in different and difficult situations and adjust well with peer groups. Neha's body, mind and relationships are all in good shape, so after the loss she has the energy, the positive outlook and the friendships she needs to lift the team.
s: A situation showing good physical well-being
The same situation shows good mental and social well-being
Explains that a healthy person copes better and adjusts well with peers, linked to the situation

questions.q:
A clipping on the class notice board reads: 'Yoga reduces anxiety and increases concentration.'
(a) Which aspect of health does reduced anxiety improve?
(b) The chapter says health and happiness are closely related. Use this to explain how feeling calmer could also help a student's physical health.
questions.a: (a) Mental well-being. (b) The chapter says being happy helps us stay active and healthy, and good health in turn improves our mood. A calmer, happier student is more likely to stay active, which helps the body, so the gain in mental well-being also supports physical well-being.
s: Part (a): mental well-being
Part (b): happiness helps us stay active and healthy, so the mental gain supports the body

questions.q:
Class 8B of a Kochi school asked all 40 classmates three questions and counted the 'yes' answers.
Question | Yes
Had no illness in the last month? | 33
Feel positive on most days? | 25
Get along well with classmates? | 31
Yes to all three questions | 19
The school's annual report later printed: '33 of our 40 students (82.5%) are healthy.'
(a) Which question checks the physical aspect, which the mental aspect and which the social aspect of health?
(b) Using the WHO definition, how many of the 40 students can be counted as healthy?
(c) Name the mistake in the annual report's reasoning and give the correct percentage of healthy students.
(d) Using the number of 'no' answers to each question, rank the three aspects from the biggest gap to the smallest, and say which aspect the school's next health programme should target first.
questions.a: (a) No illness = physical; feel positive = mental; get along = social. (b) 19, because only those who said yes to all three have complete physical, mental and social well-being. (c) The report treated 'no illness' as 'healthy', but health is not merely the absence of disease; only the 19 with all three aspects count, so the correct figure is 19/40 = 47.5%. (d) 'No' answers: mental 40 - 25 = 15, social 40 - 31 = 9, physical 40 - 33 = 7. Rank: mental, then social, then physical. The programme should target mental well-being first (for example counselling and help with coping), since that is the biggest gap.
s: Part (a): illness = physical, positive = mental, getting along = social
Part (b): 19, only those with all three
Part (c): the report counted absence of disease as health; correct figure 47.5%
Part (d): gaps 15, 9, 7 ranked mental > social > physical; target mental well-being

questions.q:
A Lucknow school plans a 'Healthiest Class' award. The only two criteria proposed are (1) the class's sports-day results and (2) how few days students were absent due to illness.
(a) Evaluate the plan: say which aspect of health the two criteria cover and which aspects they miss. (2)
(b) Propose three further criteria that the school could observe or record, each tied to an aspect from the WHO definition, and explain why the new set judges health better. (3)
questions.a: (a) Both criteria cover only the physical aspect (fitness and freedom from illness). They miss mental well-being (staying positive, coping with stress) and social well-being (getting along with classmates and others), so a class could win while many students are lonely or anxious. (b) Example criteria: how well students work together in group projects and help each other (social); whether students say they feel positive and can cope with tests or setbacks, e.g. from a short survey (mental); whether new students are included and adjust well (social). The new set matches the WHO definition of complete physical, mental and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease.
s: Both criteria cover only physical well-being
Names the missed mental and social aspects
A criterion for mental well-being
A criterion for social well-being
Explains that the full set matches all three aspects of the WHO definition

questions.q: A clinic slip lists Gauri's complaints: headache, rash, tiredness, swollen neck, dizziness, temperature of 100.5 °F, sore throat pain. Counting only what can be seen or measured, the slip lists ___ signs. (Write the number in digits.)
Nitin fell asleep on the sofa with a fever. Before the doctor arrived, his mother wrote down one observation while he was still asleep. Which observation could she have recorded without waking him?
questions.a: A thermometer reading of 102 °F
o: A thermometer reading of 102 °F
A dull ache behind both his eyes
Feeling dizzy each time he stands
Feeling very tired all morning

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Keeping our surroundings clean is part of staying healthy.
Reason (R): A person who lives in a clean place is sure to feel well, whatever her diet or relationships.
questions.a: A is true, but R is false
o: A is true, but R is false
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false, but R is true

questions.q:
A doctor examines a two-year-old who cannot yet describe how she feels.
(a) Will the doctor depend more on symptoms or on signs?
(b) Explain your choice using the difference between the two.
questions.a: (a) On signs. (b) Symptoms are what a person feels (like pain), so they must be told by the patient, and the child cannot tell them. Signs can be seen or measured by the doctor (temperature, rash, swelling), so they are still available.
s: Part (a): signs
Part (b): symptoms must be told by the patient; signs can be seen or measured by the doctor

questions.q: Children in two Kanpur colonies play outdoors every day. Colony P's ground has a garbage heap and pools of stagnant water; colony Q's ground is swept and dry. The local clinic sees more sick children from colony P. Which reason fits the chapter best?
questions.a: Dirty, unhygienic grounds are full of flies and mosquitoes
o: Dirty, unhygienic grounds are full of flies and mosquitoes
Garbage and still water are themselves the pathogens there
Colony P children must be eating more junk food every day
Uneven, dirty ground gives colony P children less exercise

questions.q: Rohit trains for two hours every evening for the district football team. He claims: 'With this much exercise I can eat fast food every day and sleep at 1 a.m. without any harm.' Is he right? Check the claim against the chapter.
questions.a: No. Exercise is only one of the habits the chapter lists. It also lists eating fast food and junk food every day and sleeping very late or not getting enough sleep as habits that are not good for health. Exercise does not cancel these: the body also needs a balanced diet and enough sleep to rest and recover.
s: Verdict: no
Daily fast food and late or short sleep are listed as unhealthy habits
Exercise does not replace a balanced diet and enough sleep for rest and recovery

questions.q:
Read three statements.
Statement 1: Limiting screen time and spending more time in nature are both part of a healthy lifestyle.
Statement 2: Air pollution from vehicles and factories can cause problems like coughing or asthma.
Statement 3: Swelling on a sprained wrist is a sign, because it can be seen.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: All three statements
o: All three statements
Statements 1 and 2 only
Statements 2 and 3 only
Statement 1 only

questions.q:
The chapter says our health depends on our lifestyle and our environment.
(a) Rani's asthma attacks increase every winter when smog covers her city. Is the main factor here her lifestyle or her environment?
(b) Her brother is tired every morning because he plays video games until 1 a.m. Which factor is it for him, and how does it differ from (a)?
questions.a: (a) Her environment: polluted air (smog) from vehicles and factories can cause coughing or asthma. (b) His lifestyle (how he lives): too much screen time and too little sleep. Unlike Rani's case, he can fix it by changing his own habit, while her trigger is in the surroundings.
s: Part (a): environment, polluted air
Part (b): lifestyle, screen time and late sleep, a habit he controls unlike the smog

questions.q:
The sick-room register of a Pune school for one morning has two columns, X and Y.
Student | Column X | Column Y
Aman | 'My head is pounding.' | Temperature 101 °F
Bela | 'I feel dizzy.' | Temperature normal; also 'feels very tired'
Chirag | 'My ankle hurts when I walk.' | Ankle swollen
Dia | 'I feel fine.' | Red rash on both arms
The school rule says: 'A student is sent home only if she shows a sign AND tells of a symptom.'
(a) Which column records symptoms and which records signs? Give the reason.
(b) One entry has been written in the wrong column. Find it and say why it does not belong there.
(c) After correcting the register, how many students show at least one sign of being unwell?
(d) Use the register to find a flaw in the school rule, and suggest a better rule.
questions.a: (a) Column X records symptoms (what the student feels and says); Column Y records signs (what can be seen or measured, such as a temperature reading or swelling). (b) 'Feels very tired' in Bela's Column Y. Tiredness is something Bela feels and tells the nurse, so it is a symptom and belongs in Column X. (c) 3: Aman (fever of 101 °F), Chirag (swelling) and Dia (rash). Bela's temperature is normal, so she shows no sign. (d) Flaw: Dia has a rash, which is a sign that she is unwell, but she reports no symptom, so the rule would keep her in class. Signs such as a rash or swelling indicate we are unwell even when we do not feel anything. Better rule: any student who shows a sign (or reports a symptom) is checked by the nurse or doctor before returning to class.
s: Part (a): X = symptoms (felt and told); Y = signs (seen or measured)
Part (b): 'feels very tired' is a symptom placed in the signs column
Part (c): 3 students (Aman, Chirag, Dia)
Part (d): Dia shows a sign without a symptom and would wrongly stay in class; a sign alone should lead to a check

questions.q:
Match each item from a Class 8 health notebook in Column I with what it is in Column II.
Column I | Column II
1. A swollen, puffy knee after a fall | a. An environmental factor affecting health
2. A stinging pain inside the ear | b. A healthy lifestyle habit
3. Thick smoke from a factory chimney near the colony | c. A sign
4. Breathing exercises such as pranayama every morning | d. A symptom

On a Delhi school's display board, a higher AQI means dirtier air. Arjun, who exercises daily and eats well, coughs through PE on a morning when the board reads 320, but not on a morning when it reads 60. Which explanation fits the chapter?
questions.a: Polluted air from vehicles and factories can cause coughing
o: Polluted air from vehicles and factories can cause coughing
His lifestyle must be poor, as lifestyle alone decides health
The cough must come from a pathogen spread by houseflies
A reading of 320 shows cleaner air, so cold air caused it

questions.q: Rakesh eats a balanced diet, sleeps by 10 p.m. and lives in a clean colony, but he has felt low and lonely since his best friend moved away. His elder sister says: 'Even with a perfect diet and enough sleep, Rakesh may keep feeling low until he spends time with friends or family.' Is her statement True or False? Give the verdict and the reason from the chapter.
questions.a: True. Health is not only about the body; feelings and relationships matter too. Even if we eat well and live in a clean place, we may not feel good if we are lonely or upset. Rakesh's diet and sleep are already fine, so what he lacks is time talking, laughing and having fun with friends and family, which keeps the mind healthy.
s: Verdict: True
Reason: a good diet and sleep do not fix loneliness; feelings and relationships matter, so time with friends and family is needed

questions.q:
Compare the two families below and analyse their health risks.
Family | Daily habits | Surroundings
The Rais | Home-cooked meals with vegetables and whole grains; evening walk; in bed by 10 p.m. | Flat next to a highway and a cement factory; frequent smoky air
The Menons | Fried snacks and sugary drinks daily; hardly any exercise; up past midnight on screens | Quiet, clean, green colony
(a) Which factor puts each family at risk: lifestyle or environment? (2)
(b) Which family can lower its risk more by its own choices, and why? (1)
(c) Suggest one change for each family that matches its risk. (2)
questions.a: (a) The Rais: environment (polluted air from vehicles and the factory can cause coughing or asthma), while their lifestyle is healthy. The Menons: lifestyle (processed, fatty and sugary food, little exercise, late nights), while their surroundings are clean. (b) The Menons, because their risk lies in how they live, which they can change themselves; the Rais' risk lies in the polluted surroundings, which their own good habits cannot fully remove. (c) Rais: e.g. check the AQI and keep the evening walk to cleaner-air times or a park. Menons: e.g. replace fried snacks and sugary drinks with a balanced diet, add daily outdoor activity and sleep earlier with less screen time.
s: Rais: environment is the risk
Menons: lifestyle is the risk
The Menons can lower risk more, as lifestyle is in their control
A fitting change for the Rais
A fitting change for the Menons

questions.q: In Sunita's city a higher AQI means dirtier air. Her brother, who eats well and exercises, coughs on the way to school on a morning when the AQI board reads 340 but not on a morning when it reads 45. His diet and habits were the same on both days, so the cause of the cough lies in his ___, not in his lifestyle. (One word: the chapter's term for a person's surroundings.)
questions.a: environment

questions.q:
A school canteen in Indore sells: a sugary cold drink, roasted chana, fried samosas, fruit chaat, a whole-wheat vegetable roll and packets of chips.
(a) Pick two items the chapter's lifestyle advice supports and two it asks us to avoid.
(b) Give the reason the chapter offers for avoiding the second group.
questions.a: (a) Support: any two of fruit chaat, whole-wheat vegetable roll, roasted chana. Avoid: any two of sugary cold drink, fried samosas, chips. (b) The chapter asks us to avoid processed, fatty or sugary food and drinks and to eat a balanced diet with fruits, vegetables and whole grains; these items are fried, sugary or processed.
s: Part (a): two suitable choices and two to avoid
Part (b): they are processed, fatty or sugary, against a balanced diet

questions.q: Sneha eats a balanced diet, does yoga every morning and lives in a clean, green colony. For two weeks after a quarrel with her best friend she has felt upset and not like herself. Which step from the chapter fits her situation best?
questions.a: Spend time talking and laughing with friends and family
o: Spend time talking and laughing with friends and family
Add more whole grains and fresh fruit to her daily meals
Check the AQI before she steps outdoors each day
Sleep later at night so she has more quiet time to think things over

questions.q: A family moves from a quiet hill town to a flat beside a busy highway and a row of small factories in an industrial area. The block's drains overflow and water collects in old tyres in the yard. Give three reasons from the chapter why the family's health may suffer here even though their diet and habits have not changed.
questions.a: (1) Smoke and dust from vehicles on the highway and from the factories pollute the air, which can cause coughing or asthma. (2) Overflowing drains and stagnant water make the place dirty and unhygienic, where flies and mosquitoes gather, and people in such areas may fall sick more often. (3) Health depends on the environment as well as on lifestyle, and clean air and water are important for health, so a good lifestyle alone cannot fully protect them.
s: Air pollution from vehicles and factories can cause coughing or asthma
Dirty surroundings with stagnant water bring flies and mosquitoes and more illness
Health depends on environment as well as lifestyle

questions.q: A new phone app advertises: 'Point your camera at your face for ten seconds and we will list every symptom you have.' Show why the app cannot do this, and say what kind of information a camera photo could give a doctor instead.
questions.a: A symptom is what a person feels, such as pain, tiredness or dizziness. These are inside the person's own experience and can only be known if the person describes them; nothing in a photo shows them. A camera records only what can be seen, so at most it could show some signs, such as a rash or swelling, which are things that can be seen or measured.
s: Symptoms are what the person feels
Feelings like pain or dizziness cannot be seen, so a photo cannot list them
A photo could show only visible signs such as a rash or swelling

questions.q: Kabir's weekday: wakes at 6:45 a.m., leaves for school without breakfast, plays games on his phone during the bus ride and again from 9 p.m. to midnight, and spends Sundays indoors. Name two habits in this routine that the chapter says are not good, and give the healthier habit the chapter suggests for each.
questions.a: Any two: skipping breakfast, replaced by eating meals regularly and a balanced diet; too much screen time, replaced by limiting screen time and spending time in nature; sleeping late or too little, replaced by getting enough sleep; staying indoors, replaced by playing outdoors or exercising.
s: First unhealthy habit with its healthier replacement
Second unhealthy habit with its healthier replacement

questions.q: Your Class 8 is running a 'Healthy Week' in a school near a busy market in Kolkata. Plan five days, one theme per day, so that together they cover: a balanced diet, physical activity and sleep, saying no to harmful substances, a clean environment, and time with friends and family. For each day give one activity and the reason from the chapter it supports.
questions.a: Any five sound days, e.g. Mon: tiffin swap of fruits, vegetables and whole grains, no packaged or fried snacks (balanced diet; avoid processed, fatty or sugary food). Tue: outdoor games plus a 'screens off by 9 p.m.' pledge (stay active, limit screen time, get enough sleep so body and mind recover). Wed: posters saying 'No' to tobacco, alcohol and addictive drugs (harmful substances). Thu: clean-up of the school ground and drains, and reading the AQI board (dirty places bring flies and mosquitoes; polluted air causes coughing or asthma). Fri: a games-and-talk afternoon with families (feelings and relationships keep our minds healthy).
s: Diet day with a chapter reason
Activity and sleep day with a chapter reason
Harmful substances day with a chapter reason
Clean environment day with a chapter reason
Friends and family day with a chapter reason

questions.q:
Rahul, a Class 8 student in Hyderabad, logged one week.
Day | Sleep (h) | Screen time (h) | Breakfast
Mon | 6 | 4 | skipped
Tue | 6 | 3.5 | skipped
Wed | 5.5 | 4 | eaten
Thu | 6 | 5 | skipped
Fri | 5 | 4.5 | skipped
Sat | 9 | 6 | eaten
Sun | 9 | 7 | eaten
He played outdoors only on Saturday, for one hour. On school nights he uses his phone in bed until about midnight, and his school bus leaves at 7 a.m. His doctor has told him he needs about 9 hours of sleep every night.
(a) Name two habits shown in the log that the chapter says are not good for health.
(b) His mother says: 'He plays outdoors on Saturday, so he is active enough.' Judge her claim using the chapter's lifestyle advice.
(c) The doctor wants him to cut weekly screen time to 20 hours by swapping it for outdoor play. On average, how many hours a day must he swap?
(d) Rahul can make only ONE change this month. Which change would improve the most entries in his log? Decide and justify.
questions.a: (a) Any two: skipping breakfast (four days), too much screen time, too little sleep on school nights (5 to 6 hours against the 9 he needs), very little outdoor activity. (b) Not right. The chapter asks us to stay physically active by playing outdoors, walking, running or cycling, and to limit screen time and spend more time in nature. One hour of play in a week, against many hours of screen time every day, is not staying active. (c) Total screen time = 4 + 3.5 + 4 + 5 + 4.5 + 6 + 7 = 34 hours; (34 - 20) / 7 = 2 hours a day. (d) Going to bed earlier on school nights, without the phone. It cuts late-night screen time, gives him enough sleep, and lets him wake in time to eat breakfast before the 7 a.m. bus, so three problems improve; a daytime screen-for-play swap would improve only screen time and activity.
s: Part (a): two unhealthy habits from the log
Part (b): not active enough; the chapter asks for regular outdoor activity and limited screen time
Part (c): 34 hours in all, so 2 hours a day
Part (d): an earlier, phone-free bedtime, as it improves sleep, breakfast and screen time together

questions.a: Frequent handwashing, no sharing of towels, covering nose and mouth

Boiling all of the hostel's drinking water and eating only well-cooked food

A doctor matches each patient's clues in Column I with the site of infection in Column II, using the chapter's table.
Column I | Column II

Six-year-old Munna in a village near Gaya often plays barefoot in a field where people defecate in the open, and he eats without washing his hands. He has worms in his stool and has stopped growing well.
(a) Name his disease and explain why the organism causing it is called a parasite.
(b) Give two ways from the chapter in which this organism could reach him.
questions.a: (a) Ascariasis (roundworm infection). The worm lives inside his body, in the intestine, and feeds on his nutrients, so it is a parasite, an organism living in or on another living being. (b) Any two: contaminated soil, contaminated food or water (e.g. eating with unwashed hands), contact with infected people or animals.

Part (b): two routes such as soil, contaminated food or water, or contact with infected people

questions.q: A Class 8 student writes in her notes: 'In Table 3.1, vaccination is listed as a preventive measure for every disease caused by a virus.' Check her note against the table and give evidence.
questions.a: Wrong. Vaccination is listed for some viral diseases, such as chickenpox, measles and hepatitis A, but not for others. For common cold and influenza the table lists handwashing, not sharing personal items and covering the mouth and nose with a mask, and for dengue it lists mosquito nets, repellents, long sleeves and control of mosquito breeding, with no vaccination.
s: Verdict: wrong
Viral diseases with vaccination listed (chickenpox, measles, hepatitis A)
Viral diseases without it (cold and influenza, dengue) and what is listed instead

questions.a: Measles

Ascariasis

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Using mosquito nets and stopping mosquito breeding around the home helps prevent both malaria and dengue.
Reason (R): Malaria is caused by a protozoan, while dengue is caused by a virus.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
o: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false

questions.q:
A science club's poster has three mistakes. Correct each one using the chapter's table.
(i) 'Tuberculosis is caused by a virus and mainly attacks the liver.'
(ii) 'Dengue spreads when people drink contaminated water.'
(iii) 'The main symptoms of cholera are itchy skin and blisters.'
questions.a: (i) Tuberculosis is caused by bacteria and mainly affects the lungs. (ii) Dengue is spread by mosquitoes (an insect-borne disease), not by water; still water only lets mosquitoes breed. (iii) Cholera causes diarrhoea and dehydration; itchy skin, rashes and blisters are symptoms of chickenpox.
s: (i) TB: bacteria, lungs
(ii) Dengue: spread by mosquitoes
(iii) Cholera: diarrhoea and dehydration

questions.q: A primary health centre's list for August: 4 cholera, 6 dengue, 3 malaria, 5 typhoid and 2 tuberculosis cases. The number of these cases whose pathogen reached the patient through a mosquito bite is ___. (Write the number in digits.)

Two classmates are absent: Simran has chickenpox and Faiz has asthma.
(a) Which of these is a communicable disease and which is non-communicable?
(b) Using (a), explain which of them the class teacher should ask to stay at home until she or he recovers, and why only that one.
questions.a: (a) Chickenpox is communicable (caused by a virus); asthma is non-communicable (not caused by a pathogen). (b) Simran. Chickenpox can spread to others, and the table lists complete isolation of the patient as a preventive measure. Faiz's asthma does not spread from one person to another, so classmates are not at risk from him.
s: Part (a): chickenpox communicable, asthma non-communicable
Part (b): Simran, as chickenpox spreads and needs isolation; asthma does not spread

questions.q:
A district health officer in Madhya Pradesh writes notes on three villages.
Village | Patients' complaints | Measures taken
Rampur | Headache, abdominal discomfort, fever and diarrhoea | Wells chlorinated
Sitapur | High fever, profuse sweating, periodic chills | Ponds drained; nets and repellents given
Khedi | Fever, sore throat, reddish rashes on the neck and ears | Patients kept apart; vaccination camp
A fourth village, Barkheda, now has six people with jaundice, nausea and pain in the upper right abdomen; its only well is beside an open drain. The officer writes: 'Sitapur's nets worked best last month, so send nets and repellents to Barkheda too.'
(a) Name Rampur's disease and the organ it infects.
(b) Name Sitapur's disease and its pathogen type.
(c) Name Khedi's disease and explain why keeping patients apart helps against it.
(d) Find the flaw in the officer's plan for Barkheda and say what should be sent instead.
questions.a: (a) Typhoid, which infects the intestine. (b) Malaria, caused by a protozoan. (c) Measles; it spreads through the air from an infected person, so keeping patients apart (isolation) stops the virus reaching others. (d) Flaw: the officer copies a measure because it worked in another village, instead of matching it to how this disease spreads. Jaundice, nausea and pain in the upper right abdomen point to hepatitis A, which infects the liver and spreads through contaminated water and food; the well beside the open drain is the likely source. Nets stop mosquitoes, which do not carry hepatitis A. A water team should be sent to clean the well and get families to drink boiled water (vaccination is also listed for hepatitis A).
s: Part (a): typhoid, intestine
Part (b): malaria, protozoan
Part (c): measles; isolation stops an air-borne disease reaching others
Part (d): the plan copies a past measure; the signs point to hepatitis A spread by water, so a water team, not nets

questions.q: A health worker in Jharkhand examines a drop of blood from a patient who has high fever, profuse sweating and chills that keep coming back. Under the microscope she sees single-celled organisms. Which conclusion fits?
questions.a: Malaria, caused by a protozoan
o: Malaria, caused by a protozoan
Dengue, caused by a protozoan
Malaria, caused by a virus
Typhoid, caused by bacteria in blood

questions.q: True or False? 'A disease that passes from one person to another must be caused by bacteria.' Give the verdict and the correction.
questions.a: False. Communicable diseases are caused by pathogens of several kinds, not only bacteria. For example, influenza, chickenpox and measles are caused by viruses and still spread from person to person; malaria is caused by a protozoan and ascariasis by worms.
s: Verdict: False
Correction: pathogens include viruses, protozoa and worms too, with an example such as chickenpox (virus)

questions.q:
Read three statements about communicable diseases.
Statement 1: Diseases caused by worms spread only through mosquito bites.
Statement 2: Houseflies that carry pathogens from garbage to uncovered food are acting as vectors.
Statement 3: Typhoid and cholera both infect the liver.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: Statement 2 only
o: Statement 2 only
Statements 1 and 2 only
Statements 2 and 3 only
All three statements

questions.q: A health worker in a Bihar village tells the gram sabha: 'If we keep our drinking water clean and boil it, we will cut down cholera, typhoid and hepatitis A, but it will not stop measles.' Check her claim against the chapter's table. Is it right, wrong or partly right?
questions.a: Right. Cholera, typhoid and hepatitis A are all spread through contaminated water and food, and boiled drinking water is listed as a preventive measure for each. Measles spreads through the air (it infects the skin and respiratory tract), so clean water does not stop it; isolation, covering the mouth and nose, hygiene and vaccination do.
s: Verdict: right
Cholera, typhoid and hepatitis A spread through contaminated water and food
Measles spreads through the air, so clean water does not stop it

questions.q:
Heavy monsoon rain floods a town in Assam. Drains overflow into open wells, rainwater stands in pits and old tyres for weeks, and hundreds of families crowd into relief camps in school halls.
(a) Predict one disease from the chapter's table likely to rise because of each of the three conditions described, and name the way it spreads. (3)
(b) For any two of your diseases, suggest one preventive step from the chapter and explain why it works. (2)
questions.a: (a) Overflowing drains in wells: contaminated water, e.g. cholera, typhoid or hepatitis A (spread through contaminated water and food). Standing water: mosquitoes breed, e.g. malaria or dengue (spread by insect vectors). Crowded camps: e.g. common cold and influenza, measles or chickenpox (spread through the air by coughs and sneezes, and by contact). (b) Example: boil drinking water, which kills or removes the pathogens before they are swallowed; empty tyres and pits and use mosquito nets, which stop vectors breeding and biting; in camps cover the mouth and nose and isolate patients, which stops air-borne pathogens reaching others.
s: Contaminated wells: a water-borne disease and its route
Standing water: a mosquito-borne disease and its route
Crowded camps: an air-borne disease and its route
First preventive step with the reason it works
Second preventive step with the reason it works

questions.q:
Two patients in a Chennai clinic both have fever. One has typhoid, the other dengue.
(a) From the chapter's table, give one symptom that would point to dengue and one that would point to typhoid.
(b) Why should the advice on prevention given to their families be different?
questions.a: (a) Dengue: muscle and joint pain (or nausea with headache). Typhoid: abdominal discomfort and diarrhoea. (b) Dengue is spread by mosquitoes, so its family needs nets, repellents, long sleeves and no still water. Typhoid spreads through contaminated water and food, so its family needs boiled water, properly cooked food and good hygiene and sanitation.
s: Part (a): a dengue symptom and a typhoid symptom from the table
Part (b): mosquito control for dengue versus clean water and food for typhoid

questions.q: Tara's sister has a contagious infection. Tara never touches her, but she uses her sister's towel and handkerchief for two days and then falls ill with the same disease. How did the pathogen most likely reach Tara?
questions.a: Indirect contact through shared personal items
o: Indirect contact through shared personal items
Direct contact, such as shaking hands
A vector such as a mosquito or a housefly carrying it
Drinking water that had been contaminated

questions.q: The answer to a question is: 'Use mosquito nets and repellents, and do not let water collect in coolers and pots.' Write a question, set in a real situation, for which this is the correct answer. Then name the two diseases in the chapter this protects against and the type of pathogen behind each.
questions.a: Example question: 'Cases of high fever with chills and of fever with joint pain are rising in our colony after the rains. What should families do?' Diseases: malaria, caused by a protozoan, and dengue, caused by a virus; both are carried by mosquitoes, which breed in still water.
s: A sensible question where mosquito control is the answer
Names malaria and dengue
Malaria: protozoan; dengue: virus

questions.q:
A municipal worker clears a blocked sewer line in the morning and then eats his lunch without washing his hands. Two days later he has severe diarrhoea and dehydration, and a lab test of his stool finds the bacteria that cause his illness.
(a) Trace, step by step, how the pathogen most likely got from the sewer into the organ it infects.
(b) Which one habit from the chapter would have broken this chain, and at which step?
questions.a: (a) The sewage carried cholera bacteria; they got onto his hands while working; from his hands they got onto his food; he swallowed them with the food, and they infected his intestine, causing diarrhoea and dehydration (cholera). (b) Washing his hands with soap and water before eating. It removes pathogens from the hands, so the chain breaks at the step where the bacteria pass from his hands to his food.
s: Part (a): sewage to hands to food to intestine, naming cholera or bacteria
Part (b): handwashing with soap and water, breaking the hands-to-food step

questions.q:
A resident welfare association in Bengaluru gets weekly figures from its colony clinic during the monsoon.
Week | Dengue cases | Cholera cases
1 | 4 | 1
2 | 7 | 2
3 | 14 | 4
4 | 28 | 8
Residents have noticed water standing in coolers, flower pots and a construction pit. The colony's drinking-water tank was also found uncovered last month.
(a) Which of the two diseases is spread by a vector, and what is the vector?
(b) A resident says: 'Both diseases are coming from the water standing in the coolers.' Judge this using how each disease spreads.
(c) From week 2 on, both diseases have doubled every week. If this continues, how many cases of each are expected in week 5, and which disease would add more new cases?
(d) This week the association can afford only one drive: emptying coolers, pots and the pit across the colony, or a boil-your-water and handwashing campaign. Both have been doubling since week 2. Decide which drive to run first and justify it from your answers to (b) and (c).
questions.a: (a) Dengue; it is spread by mosquitoes, which act as vectors. (b) Only partly right. Standing water lets the mosquitoes that carry dengue breed, so it is linked to dengue. Cholera is not spread by mosquitoes; it spreads through contaminated drinking water and food (here the uncovered tank is a likelier source). (c) Dengue 28 x 2 = 56; cholera 8 x 2 = 16. Dengue would add 28 new cases, cholera 8, so dengue adds more. (d) Emptying the standing water first. Both diseases double each week, but dengue is adding far more cases (28 against 8 next week), and the still water is where its mosquito vectors breed; handwashing and boiled water do nothing against mosquito bites. Cholera still needs attention, so families should be asked to boil drinking water and the tank covered as soon as possible.
s: Part (a): dengue, mosquitoes as vectors
Part (b): partly right; still water breeds dengue mosquitoes but cholera spreads through contaminated water and food
Part (c): 56 dengue and 16 cholera; dengue adds more
Part (d): the still-water drive first, as dengue adds more cases and handwashing does not stop mosquitoes, with cholera noted

questions.q: Make a yes/no key, as a numbered set of questions, that a health volunteer could use to tell these five diseases apart: tuberculosis, hepatitis A, cholera, malaria and dengue. Each question must use a fact from the chapter's table (causal agent, site of infection, symptoms or way of spreading). Show where each disease ends up in your key.
questions.a: One possible key: 1. Is it spread by insects (mosquitoes)? Yes: go to 2. No: go to 3. 2. Is the causal agent a protozoan? Yes: malaria. No (a virus): dengue. 3. Does it spread through the air and infect the lungs? Yes: tuberculosis. No (water and food): go to 4. 4. Does it infect the liver and cause jaundice? Yes: hepatitis A. No (intestine, diarrhoea and dehydration): cholera. Any key that separates all five correctly with table facts earns the marks.
s: A first question that splits the group correctly on a table fact
Malaria and dengue separated by a correct fact
Tuberculosis separated by a correct fact
Hepatitis A and cholera separated by a correct fact
Every disease ends in exactly one place in the key

questions.q:
Smallpox and polio cases are now rare in India, but diabetes and heart problems are common.
(a) Give one reason from the chapter why diseases like polio have become rare.
(b) Give one reason from the chapter why diseases like diabetes have become more common, and say why the reason in (a) cannot stop them.
questions.a: (a) Vaccines: children are given drops or injections that protect them from diseases such as polio, and mass vaccination eradicated smallpox. (b) Changes in how people live, such as eating more processed food, getting less exercise and living longer lives. Vaccines work by training the immune system against pathogens, but diabetes and heart disease are non-communicable and are not caused by pathogens, so vaccines cannot prevent them.
s: Part (a): vaccination
Part (b): lifestyle change; vaccines act against pathogens and NCDs have none

questions.q: A doctor at a Lucknow clinic sees four patients. Which of them has a chronic disease as the chapter uses the word?

o: Asthma attacks on and off for the past two years
A cold that cleared up completely after six days

A chickenpox rash that healed within a fortnight

questions.q:
Read three statements about non-communicable diseases.
Statement 1: Goitre can spread from person to person in crowded places.
Statement 2: Diabetes often develops from a combination of hormonal imbalance and reasons such as lack of physical activity.
Statement 3: Cancer is both a non-communicable disease and, as it often lasts more than three months, a chronic disease.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: Statements 2 and 3 only
o: Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 1 and 2 only
Statement 3 only
All three statements

questions.q: A girl in a Ranchi hostel ate almost the same plain meal every day for months. A blood test now shows anaemia, and no pathogen is found. How should her disease be grouped?
questions.a: Non-communicable, a deficiency disease
o: Non-communicable, a deficiency disease
Communicable, spread by sharing plates
Communicable, carried by hostel flies
